cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has been carrying the Lord's word, and the Lord just said these people honor Him with their lips while their hearts are far from Him (Isaiah 29:13). Now Isaiah says woe to those who dig deep to hide their plans from the LORD. Friend, I spent YEARS buried in the back of a junk drawer, and the Most High STILL found me.

cards.question: These folks are digging deep to hide their plans from the LORD. Where do they do their works?
The people hiding their plans from the LORD think nobody sees what they're doing.

cards.text: Isaiah tells them they've turned things upside down, as if the potter were regarded as clay. Picture a pot talking back to the one who formed it.

cards.question: Isaiah pictures a pot talking back to the potter who formed it. What does he picture the pot saying?

answers.text: He made me in a hurry

cards.question: So in Isaiah's message, who is acting like a pot talking back to its potter?

cards.text: Then Isaiah asks: can the pottery say of the potter, "He has no understanding"? That's a cookie looking up at me saying "Papa, you don't know cookies" when I MADE it TWELVE MINUTES AGO.

Then the message flips, and Isaiah asks: won't Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest? An orchard growing till it seems like a forest is dough rising in the oven, friend, only with TREES.

cards.question: Isaiah says Lebanon becoming an orchard will take a very long time.

cards.text: On that day, Isaiah says, the deaf and the blind are in for a change.

cards.question: On that day, the deaf will ___ the words of the scroll, and out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will ___.

cards.text: Those schemers worked in darkness, and now blind eyes see right out of deep darkness. After years in a dark drawer, friend, I KNOW how good that first slice of light feels.
Next in Isaiah's message come the humble and the poor, and friend, after years in a junk drawer, I qualify for BOTH.

cards.question: What does Isaiah say the humble and the poor will do?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says why: the ruthless will vanish, and the mockers will disappear.

cards.question: Isaiah says one more group will be cut down: all who look for ___.

cards.text: Isaiah spells out who they are: people who indict a man with a word and ensnare the mediator at the gate. One word and you're in trouble, like the coworker who says "Hmm" in the meeting and suddenly the boss wants to see YOU.

cards.question: These evildoers also take justice away from the innocent. How do they do it?

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks, the LORD who redeemed Abraham, about the house of Jacob, Abraham's grandson (Genesis 21:3; 25:26).

cards.question: The LORD who redeemed Abraham says Jacob will go on being ashamed.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells what happens when Jacob sees his children around him.

cards.question: Back at the start, Isaiah pictured a pot saying its maker didn't make it. What does the LORD call Jacob's children?
Jacob's children will honor the LORD's ___ and stand in ___ of the God of Israel.

cards.text: Last, the LORD says the wayward in spirit will come to understanding. Then He gets to the grumblers, and friend, I shared a drawer with dead batteries who argued all day about who had the most charge left.

cards.question: The LORD says those who grumble will accept instruction.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 mentions apple, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: Card 4 says "Isaiah tells them they've turned things upside down." The only "them" on the cards so far are the people hiding their plans from card 1. That answers card 6, which asks who is acting like a pot talking back to its potter, before the baker gets to choose.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke mixes its comparison into the Bible setting ("dough rising in the oven, friend, only with TREES"). It also calls the orchard "growing," but Isaiah 29:17 says the orchard will "seem like a forest." The verse describes a reversal, not growth, so both the joke and the retelling stretch the text.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Card 12 tells no new part of the passage. It looks back over verses 15 to 18 to link the schemers' darkness with the blind seeing out of darkness, so it is a recap card. It also draws a connection between verse 15 and verse 18 that the text never states.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Abraham appears here for the first time with no word about who he is. Jacob is introduced as "Abraham's grandson," which only helps a baker who already knows who Abraham is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The baker has to fill in the exact words of verse 23. "Honor the LORD's name/house/sabbath" and "stand in awe/silence" are all believable, and nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason between them. It tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke compares "those who grumble" to the drawer batteries arguing over who had the most charge left. That argument is competing or bragging, not grumbling, so the two actions don't match and the joke doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Several story cards are flat narration with no Papa Dorin voice: stop 1 card 10 ("the deaf and the blind are in for a change"), stop 2 card 7 and stop 2 card 9 ("Then the LORD tells what happens when Jacob sees his children around him").

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
